short: The (110) and (320) surfaces of a Cantor alloy
title: The (110) and (320) surfaces of a Cantor alloy

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: The surface composition and atomic structure of the Cantor alloy FeCrMnNiCo are undetermined. Repeated annealing in this temperature range could decompose the single-phase solid solution into (inter)metallic phases.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/gap), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/variable_sweep), n5 (PRC/treatment). Premises: Earlier studies [25-27] annealed Cantor alloys over a comparable temperature range

states.title: Structure state
states.head: The annealed surface is Ni- and Mn-enriched: Mn triples to ~24 at.% and Ni reaches ~38 at.% in the topmost layers. Above ~873 K the surface Mn content collapses.
states.detail: Absorbed: n6 (STR/chemistry/composition), n7 (STR/chemistry/composition), n9 (STR/microstructure/shape), n10 (STR/phase/identity), n11 (STR/phase/identity), n12 (STR/microstructure/shape), n15 (STR/microstructure/shape), n13 (STR/phase/identity), n14 (STR/chemistry/composition). Premises: FeCrMnNiCo is fcc with a = 3.596 A, giving a (110) interlayer spacing of 1.27 A and d(320) = 1.0 A (half-step 0.5 A)

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Annealing drives Ni and Mn to segregate to the surface in equal amounts, a surface rather than grain-boundary process. The Mn loss above 873 K is desorption from the surface, not diffusion into the bulk.
states.detail: Absorbed: m1 (MEC/pathway), m2 (MEC/identification), m3 (MEC/pathway), p1 (PRP/value), p2 (PRP/value). Premises: fcc(320) surface model: primitive mesh 6.73 x 3.60 A (alpha = 105.5 deg), centred mesh 12.97 x 3.60 A, rows spaced 6.48 A

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: The Cantor alloy keeps a homogeneous fcc bulk but develops a Ni/Mn-enriched surface whose structure depends on grain orientation

nodes.title: TEM:HAADF, F6
nodes.head: The SAED inset is one square array of sharp spots indexed 020 and 002, i.e. a single fcc phase
nodes.solves: Bulk and subsurface remain a single fcc phase after the annealing cycles; no precipitates form
nodes.note: '020' and '002' are printed on the inset; the 3.6 A cell and the 150 nm aperture are text-only. The HAADF panel itself shows an unbroken lattice with uniform contrast and no second phase
nodes.detail: o22: The SAED inset is one square array of sharp spots indexed 020 and 002, i.e. a single fcc phase
